objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a breast mass.

turns.content: Doctor: Hello—I'm Dr. Agent. To evaluate your breast mass, I need to ask: how old are you, and when did you first notice the lump?
Patient: I’m 33 years old, and I first noticed the lump about three weeks ago. It’s on my right breast and it hasn’t changed in size since then.

Doctor: Any pain, redness, warmth, or nipple discharge/skin dimpling, and does the lump feel mobile or fixed to the skin/chest wall? Doctor: Also, do you have any fever, recent pregnancy/breastfeeding, or a known family history of breast/ovarian cancer? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Targeted_Breast_Ultrasound_(Right)

RESULTS: Vital signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Breast exam (right): No skin changes or nipple discharge; 2.5-cm rubbery, mobile, nontender mass in upper outer quadrant; no axillary lymphadenopathy. Targeted right breast ultrasound: 2.5-cm well-circumscribed, solid mass without suspicious features. Biopsy histopathology: Rounded contour with overgrowth of fibrous and glandular tissue.

Doctor: Given your age (33) and the exam/ultrasound showing a well-circumscribed, mobile, nontender solid mass, and the biopsy description of fibrous-and-glandular overgrowth with a rounded contour, this most strongly fits a benign fibroadenoma. Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Fibroadenoma (benign breast tumor)
